title: Too Hot to Touch
text:
Upon opening the box, I assumed I was getting a steal of a deal with how fancy the box looked. Then, there was a box within that box that looked just as nice. I was very impressed by the packaging. The box included the hair dyer, two different end caps, and a piece of paper with description, instructions, warranty info, etc.

The instructions didn’t really give much useful information. Nowhere on the piece of paper did it mention why you would choose to use one head attachment over the other. The biggest confusion was having no description as to what the buttons on the hair dryer were for. The images on the instructions did not match what was on the hair dryer. (See picture of the buttons – the two larger buttons both have the same symbols with no description)

I put one of the head attachments on the hair dryer, then plugged the unit in. It immediately started running, so I had to use the trial and error method of figuring out which button controlled the speed and which button controlled the heat. The hair dryer had a good weight to it and wasn’t difficult to continually hold up to dry my hair. I’ve got medium length, fine/thin hair, and it took a little over 6 minutes to fully dry my hair. While using the hair dryer, and especially after turning it off, the black end attachment was extremely hot to the touch.

Comparing to a Revlon hair dryer of the same wattage, they are almost identical in size. When using the same hot/high dry setting, the Revlon hair dryer only took about 4 ½ minutes to dry my hair. Not a huge difference, but worth mentioning. They both have around the same loudness while running. The most important difference between the two hair dryers was the temperature of the end cap attachments after using to dry my hair. The Revlon hair dryer’s end cap was 143F after I finished drying my hair, while the xtava peony hair dryer’s end cap was 256F!

Overall, this hair dryer is just okay. It’s a good basic hair dryer, but I don’t know that I would pick it to use every day. The generic buttons on the machine and lack of instructions on what they were for was annoying, but obviously could be figured out after one use. I’m more disappointed in how dangerously hot the end piece gets after using it for just a few minutes of use. I typically have to switch positions of hair tools in my hands when I’m drying my right side vs my left side, but with how hot that end piece gets, it’s not practical to touch it to rotate it. I would hate for my toddler to get ahold of it after I use it and hurt himself (yes, you’re supposed to keep it out of reach of kids, but anyone with young kids knows how fast their little hands start feeling around on the counters as far as they can reach). If you don’t have young kids and have a high heat tolerance, the temperature of the unit while/after using likely wouldn’t be an issue, but for me, it’s a deal breaker.

title: Truly some wonderful stuff to fight "winter hands"
text:
I hate winter for a lot of reasons, but one of them is that my hands get so dry that I get cracks at my fingertips. It’s annoying and painful, especially at night. I’ve tried all sorts of moisturizers without much success. The best results (if you can call it that) have been from using petroleum jelly, but that’s messy and it still doesn’t work well.

This argan oil, however, has been hugely effective. It gave me results right from the first day, and over the course of just a few days I can see noticeable healing of the skin cracks. No more pain and my hands feel far better than any other treatment I’ve tried.

The product comes very nicely packaged, with a nice box filled with shredded packing material to keep the glass bottle safe in transit. It also makes for a very nice presentation should you want to give this as a gift. The bottle comes with a dropper and a “spritz” head. The latter is my only quibble – the spray head didn’t work well at all, and made sort of a mess when using it to dispense the oil. I replaced it with the dropper and had much better results.

The oil itself has little or no scent. You need very, very little for results – I use about 1-2 small drops per hand, and that’s more than enough. It spreads easily (as expected given that it’s oil). It does take a few minutes to soak in – my hands are very greasy when I first apply it, but after a few minutes the greasiness goes away. The sheen from the oil stays around longer, but that too dissipates after 30 minutes or so.

This can be used for a wide range of applications including face, body and even hair. It comes with a good amount of information to help explain how/where to use it, and how the oil was processed.

I’m very impressed with this oil – it’s the only product I’ve ever tried that totally worked to solve my dry/cracked hands. It’s not cheap, but well worth the price if you need a highly effective moisturizer. Highly recommend.

title: Inconsistent/Changed Formula was Problematic
text:
The first time I purchased this, I loved it. It felt great, smelled good, and worked nicely to get away from regular deodorant/antiperspirant. I was really pleased with the product - never had a problem with staining, only a very minor reddening of the skin on one armpit during the first week of use and no further skin reactions or anything other than a pleasant experience. My second purchase didn't go so well. The first thing I noticed was that where the first jar had been perfectly smooth, the new one seemed more gritty or clumpy. I let it warm some and mixed it around to improve consistency, and things seemed OK until I was doing laundry and realized I had ruined two nice shirts with disgusting, oily stains - something that never happened the first time around. This just seems weird to me, because I would assume the second jar with its grittier, dryer composition would be less oily.

I reduced the amount I was using even further and made sure it had absorbed more fully before putting on a shirt, and things seemed better for the next week. Then my armpits started breaking out with a painful, blistering rash. Again, something I never experienced with the first jar.

I threw the second one away, and won't be purchasing this product again. The first experience was great, but the changed formula--or perhaps it didn't change and it's just inconsistent across batches--was awful. It took a couple of weeks for the rash this caused to go away, which was painful, embarrassing and inconvenient.

title: Great Anti-Aging Product-Leaves Smooth Skin-Tips for Application and Use Information!
text:
I am very pleased so far with the InterSight Naturals Hyaluronic Acid so far. It comes in a 1 oz bottle but a little goes a long way. I will explain in my review.

There are a lot of benefits in general to your body with Hyaluronic Acid, including your skin and face. The major benefit is that it is an anti-aging agent. We already have this in our skin. As we age, we lose some along with collagen. Hyaluronic Acid in this Serum allows your skin to retain more moisture, whether you have oily skin or not. It has a lightweight texture and works for oily or dry skin and sensitive skin too. That's great because I personally have all of that going on with my face.

There are other serums out there similar to this. I like InterSight's Hyaluronic Acid because it is free of fragrance/scent and drying agents like alcohol. It's ingredients include (of course) hyaluronic acid, witch hazel, green tea, jojoba oil, vitamins c and e and aloe. So, if you are familiar with any of these you will know that these are elements are soothing to the skin and each have their own benefits. I like products that have natural ingredients versus a lot of chemicals that I don't know how to pronounce.

This product is advertised to activate collagen production, which is what the h. acid does. It goes beneath the skin's surface when applied correctly and retains moisture, plumping it up like youthful skin. When I use this, I notice that my skin appearance is very youthful and fresh. You can use your own moisturizer afterwards (I switch it up personally but mainly use Vanicream Light Lotion, not cream, because it's "Dye free, perfume/fragrance free, lanolin free, paraben free, formaldehyde free." Also, it isn't greasy.)

This bottle comes with a dropper in it. I have a few tips if it will help anyone for use.

2. Apply the product. I found that it's easier and less waste to put three drops on my left 3 finger pads - ring, middle and pointer finger, share some with the same fingers on the right hand and apply with an upward direction starting with the décolletage and neck area.
*Note - a little goes a long way. I used less than half a dropperful for 1 treatment.

I use Elta MD UV Shield Broad Spectrum SPF 45, the transparent version for a lot of reasons. Product is great, non-greasy, soaks in, is for the face and body, cost is reasonable, no scent and it protects my skin! One last tip in case you don't know why you should use it on your décolletage, neck in addition to the face. Guess where aging shows the most? The neck and, not listed prior, your hands! Neck wise-look at people and their necks. The age usually shows up sooner. So, it's important to include it. When you put sunscreen on, consider putting it on your hands too, or for that matter, your arms, especially the side that faces the window when you ride in a car.

I wanted to upgrade to a beard-oriented product to keep the softness and help tame fly-aways (and avoid my g/f's ire), so I decided to try this, along with adding a beard brush. As a face wash/shampoo, it's fine -- it cleans well and the smell is light and neutral (pleasantly reminds me of the old-school barbershop that cut my hair when I was a kid). However, I was very disappointed by the conditioning (or lack thereof). Even after two weeks of use, my beard just wasn't as soft, and I had more fly-aways than before. I tried washing and rinsing, as well as leaving it in for a couple of minutes before rinsing, and found no difference. As a test, I used the other conditioner again after this, and softness returned, which suggests this product doesn't have sufficient quantities of the "conditioning" ingredients and is really more of a 2-in-1 face wash/shampoo.

Ultimately I wanted to like this, but I found I get the same results with my normal (not-beard-oriented) moisturizing face wash + beard brush, as I do with this product + beard brush, at less than half the price. So, if you need beard conditioning, look elsewhere, or plan to add another product at additional cost (I now see this brand makes a separate beard moisturizer / leave-in conditioner product.)

However, if you don't currently have any sort of face wash and suffer from "beardruff" or itching, this will probably help you, albeit at a premium price. Side note, the packaging is good and thoughtfully includes both a pump-type and a flip-up cap to accommodate your shower or travel preferences.

title: Long time blade user switches to electric
text:
This review is being written by my Husband.

The Norelco 1050 is my first electric shaver. I've been using blades since I first started shaving. I'm now in my mid 40's. I've now been using this shaver exclusively for the last two weeks. All-in-all it is pretty good. Does it give me as close a shave as I got with a blade - no, but it does get pretty close and the advantages I'm about to tell you about make it worth while.

Over the last few years, I swear my whiskers have felt like they were turning into wire. With the blade it was taking me about 30 minutes in front of a mirror to shave. I would pull the skin in all kinds of directions and drag the blade over the skin in all kinds of directions. I got into the habit of shaving using water alone first, followed by dry, followed by an aloe lotion. By the time I was done with the blade, I had a super close shave. However, if I was using a new blade, I would frequently have several deep cuts and nicks. So, I would shave very carefully until the blade was dull. A dull blade reduced the amount of deep cuts and nicks (but I would still have some to several) but also increased the time required to shave. Years ago, it would take about a week for the blade to dull enough but, once dull enough, I could use that blade for a month or more before having to switch blades. Lately, it would take a few days to dull but would only last a few days. So, getting cut to ribbons much more frequently is what prompted me to try an electric.

The first few days to week with the electric, I was convinced I would be returning it. During the second week, my attitude changed. It still took up to 30 minutes to get a shave I was comfortable with. I still pull my skin in all kind of directions and run the shaver in all kinds of directions just like I did with the blade. However, as my face has become accustomed to the electric, the time has come down some to around 20 minutes. I think it may come down a little more as time goes by. Parts of my face get a shave as close as I got with the blade, especially the mustache zone, under the lower lip, and my cheeks. My chin gets close. My neck and the lower jaw (transition from face to neck) are the worst. However, they are close to what I would get when using a new blade and had to be very careful to prevent gouging my face.

The pleasant items about using the electric include: I have only gotten two small nicks in two weeks. I only have to spend a minute in front of the mirror to shave around the sideburns (to prevent shaving too high on the cheek) - the rest of the time I can walk around or watch TV. Cleanup is a snap - pop open the three chambers and rinse with hot water. The razor burn I had on my right lower jaw bone (which I didn't attribute to razor burn but thought it was a skin condition) is almost gone.

In the first few minutes, the shaver gets the bulk of the whiskers; the remaining time is trying to get a closer shave. There is a diminishing point of return on time verses close shave which is why I think the shaving time will come down as I decide where that point is.

Since using the electric, my wife said she thinks my face looks better (I think because of the bumps on the right lower jaw bone going away). She also thinks it feels as smooth as it did with the blade even though I can feel where the whiskers haven't been completely eliminated.

So, end result - not a close as a blade but pretty close with some nice benefits that make it worth continuing to use instead of going back to a blade.

title: No Norelco, I still prefer my 550 TL
text:

When I had the chance to try the Norelco Cool Skin 8040X, I looked forward to putting this Norelco newbie through its paces.

But I was very disappointed.

THe VERY first thing I DID NOT like (ZERO stars for this!!) was the plastic "Clamshell Packaging" -- which is a waste of plastic and time. IF Norelco had decided to incorporate a Travel Case into this Clamshell packaging with re-usable features, then I would have been content. But as it was, this was just a waste of plastic. Clamshell packages have sent numerous folks to the hospital with some nasty cuts inflicted while trying to open this sealed, thick plastic, stubborn packaging. Then again, it is a waste of plastics made even more wasteful when you consider the price of petroleum nowadays, and the inability to recycle this type of plastic. I suppose someone who wants to, can, with a little ingenuity and transparent mailing tape, take this Clamshell Package and create a travel container for their 8040x-- which might be a good idea, because the fabric travel pouch that Norelco supplies with this shaver only holds the shaver, and not the accessories -- unless you want to cram everything into the travel case and NOT close it.

Well.... now -- about the shaver itself. The instruction book is very thorough -- but the warnings interspersed throughout are in grey print -- how about bold black?

The shaver itself is nothing I would want to use all the time -- in fact, after trying it, I still prefer my 550 TL. The heads on the 8040X DO flex, but the moisturizing cream/gel only comes through two of them when all three heads with moisturizer would work much better -- the heads also drag across my skin -- and in some instances gave me a bit of razor burn -- especially on my neck. This shaver was used in the shower, so there was plenty of (acqua) moisture, in addition to gel moisturizer, available for a close shave, but the shave was not as good as it should have been.

Putting the moisturizer into the shaver is a feat that involves pumping the cartridge manually and then cleaning up the excess moisturizer that suddenly splats out of the shaver when it is full. Um.........

This Norelco 8040X is a nice idea, but it's gimmicky and labor intensive, when all I want is a quick shave and then a quick rinse of the heads and the knowledge that my shaver will be ready and willing the next morning. The Norelco 8040X IMHO probably work just as well on dry skin as on wet -- but it's nothing I would want to use on a regular basis.

I've never used 'beard oil' before, so just for the helluvit decided to give some a try, and grabbed the trial pack (original scent).

The Balm:
This is pretty much just greasy. Feels and smells mostly like you're just rubbing Vaseline on your beard, though a bit lighter.

The package:
The presentation is actually really nice. Nice little velvet bag with a string, the balm/oil, and even a guitar pick.

The result:

The price:
Here's probably the bigger issue; it's around $6 for this trial, and you really only get about 1, maybe 1.5 uses out of the teeny tiny sample of oil (see pic). I actually feel like I got a little bit ripped off on the price for the amount you get. I'd like to see the trial priced more around the 3/4 dollar mark in total (incl. shipping, et. al.). I'd like to try some different scents, but there's not a chance in Hell I'm paying that amount again for even 1 more sample for that amount of oil, and there're a whole lot of scents to try before you find one that you might like. On the other hand, I saw they offer a trial package of all scents (the same tiny sized bottles), which is cool, but it's $30+ .... no thanks. Drop it to around $10 total and I'll try it. I'd also like to see them offer that same package, minus everything but the oils (no balms, etc.), just to see which scent I like, and make it around say $5 total.

All-in-all:
It's "ok". If I could find the scent that I like w/out dropping a fortune in the process, I'd probably buy the big bottle of it, or even bottle(S) if I found more than 1 scent I liked; possibly regularly. But currently, I think I'll just skip it.

title: Would Be Better With Low Battery Indicator
text:
I've been using this shaver for about a month now, and find its performance to be somewhat better than my previous Norelco shaver (5822) at this price point. Not having a low battery indicator is the most serious deficiency of the 7140.

The instructions state: "Battery performance is best if you recharge only when the batteries are (almost) completely empty."

If you follow this advice, it means you'll have a bad shave or two as the battery runs down, and then have to use it as a corded razor on the day it really slows down. At least the AC adapter bypasses the battery charger when using it corded, so this will not further degrade the battery. Another reviewer commented Norelco's web site says the battery is NiMH, which is supported by the fact there is no NiCd warning on the outside of the 7140 (like there is on the 5822). So fully discharging the batteries before recharging may not be that important.

This is my first Norelco with a washable shave head. I am so far very satisfied with this feature, and consider it one reason the shaver delivers consistently close shaves.

I would have deducted two stars for the lack of a low battery indicator, were it not for the apparent use of NiMH batteries and the effectiveness of wash-through cleaning of the shave head. Other than that, it is what I expected with respect to operating noise, weight, trimmer, etc. One thing to note: it does not come with a case of any kind; just a plastic blade protector.

About me: I have been shaving with electric razors for about 30 years. I started with Norelco rotary, tried Remington foil, Braun foil, and then eventually back to Norelco rotary probably 15 years ago. Therefore my face is well conditioned for this shaver. However, if I go more than a couple days without shaving, I "pay for it" when the electric razor has trouble with relatively long whiskers - a lot of pulling along with the cutting. I generally replace the blades once a year, and don't disassemble and clean them as often as I should (instructions recommend montly).

Original Review:

I have used several electric shavers in my life, all of them being Norelco. I was never a fan of the two-bladed shavers, I grow a thick beard, and it just takes too long to shave with those things. The 3-bladed shavers can be hit or miss depending on brand/model. Norelco used to make quality shavers back in the 80's and 90's. Since Phillips's acquisition of the Norelco brand however, the quality has gone down drastically. Many reviews complain of underpowered motors, motors burning out early, and poor shaving quality, unless of course you buy the high end 200 dollar model, then your in heaven lol.

Thankfully these day, we have a choice. I don't know about you, but I am not in the rich income bracket, I can't just dump 200 dollars into a shaver just to get something that is quality. Fortunately, there are many different types of shavers made in China now, that are much more affordable. What sold me on this shaver, is that it uses a 800MAH lithium rechargeable battery, that can be charged via USB. It uses a pretty blue LED battery indicator display, which shows minutes of run-time remaining.

It uses a standard 3-bladed system, with a pop up side-burn trimmer. It is also easy to pop the blades off and clean them, and even though I didn't require this feature, it is also IPX7 waterproof. The shaver comes with a nice velvet pouch, a brush, USB cable, and a operators manual. When I turned the unit on, I couldn't believe how quiet this thing runs, most certainly quieter then the old 80's - 90's Norelco models. So the question you might be asking is, how does it perform?

If all you have is stubble, you can expect this to provide a pretty smooth shave within a reasonable amount of time. I just did nice and slow rotational movements, as you are supposed to do with this type of shaver, and it did a pretty good job! If you let your beard get beyond a stubble, as one would expect, it does take longer to get the job done, but the shaver was able to do it, and seemed to have enough power, not just in time duration, but also in horse power.

Since I did not do a wet shave with this, I can't speak as to its effectiveness. I bought an electric shaver for the convenience of a dry shave, as wet shaving is a pain in the but for me. While the water proof rating allows one to simply run the head under the water stream to clean it out, I however just used the brush that they supplied, and some canned air, and it did just as good, without fully taking the blades out of the head. Recharge time is faster then they state when utilizing a powerful Anker wall charger that puts out 3 amps. I charged my battery from 45 minutes left, to 60-minutes left, in only 20 minutes.

In conclusion, I believe this to be a very nice electric shaver. And for the price I paid for it, I expected it to be weaker in construction, however, that is further from the truth. The construction of this shaver is top notch, and rivals higher end Phillips Norelco's in my humble opinion. If you need a quality electric shaver that will get the job done, and doesn't break the bank, I highly recommend this one! 5 out of 5 stars!

title: Better than WEN for multi-texture black hair
text:
Let me start of by saying I use this product alone now for everyone in the house for co-washing. I have relaxed hair that I am trying to transition back to natural. One has very kinky coiled low porous hair that is actually very long when braided but is the type of hair that has a lot of shrinkage and my other daughter has kind of loose wavy curls but with lots of frizz.

All of us have long hair and I used to use WEN or the generic version called Just One or one from Sally's for years. Both are expensive. WEN is really ridiculous on the price and for our hair at least I had to use a lot to get it slippery. Lots of times the WEN left my own hair feeling kind of stripped. It has completely replaced WEN/Just One. It really does moisturize/condition the hair, not just detangle.

I use this three different ways. First just as it's advertised which is a co-wash. Great for when the hair is not very dirty and you don't need to use a clarifying shampoo. I will say that I had to apply it a bit differently to my middle baby girls hair to get the best slippage and moisturizing. I think it's because like I said, her hair is not very porous. With her hair I have to get it very wet with water a bit hotter than I use on the others, usually I start mid length and apply downward to the ends and then add some to the roots but on her I have to add a bit to the roots first after sectioning it, Then massage like I would when shampooing, then rinse just a bit then apply the rest from end up to scalp and doing it that way for some reason makes the comb out easy.Then I follow with a rinse and go through the normal conditioning process. Secondly I use it as a detangling conditioner after doing a clarifying shampoo. When I use it this way I rinse some of it out after combing, add my other conditioning products and basically sit under a hot cap making it a deep conditioner. and the third way I use this is heavily diluted in a spray bottle of water, like maybe a tablespoon in a smaller spray bottle basically to refresh and re-moisturize my younger girls braid out styles. Lots of times I do it that way before bed. It works great, detangles, good slippage, makes it easy to comb/brush out any dirt or dust that may have got on the hair and a great way to add your butters and sealing oils instead of on dry hair, which may work for some but I have never had luck adding oils to mine or my girls hair while it was dry. I usually only need one bottle of this the whole month.

This product has especially made a huge difference in the condition of my oldest daughters relaxed hair. It is now very healthy where before it was so dry. She was having breakage before. Her hair was like straw at the ends.This and another product that has really combated her dryness is called Olive Cream by Hollywood beauty. It is water based so some people may not want to use it as a hairdressing on already flat ironed or hair that has already been styled for the day,but that stuff works great on her hair.

I know hair is one of those things that's different for everyone so what this has done for us may not work for you or yours but for the price you can't really go wrong in at least giving it a try.

As for this stuff by Pantene, I just pray they DO NOT CHANGE THEIR FORMULA! It works great for us just the way it is.

title: These Fun Rods Will Deliver Curls
text:
I've used these flexible curling rods several times now. First, I practiced wrapping my hair up a few times at home without waiting the required time to get the curls. (I was so excited to try it out when they arrived.) I also tried it with both wet and dry hair. The hair wrapping goes pretty quickly because there are no fasteners or clips to worry about. That was a key factor in my decision to try these. You just roll up the hair from the bottom up and then bend the long ends up over the curl to secure. And they do stay put, once you figure out which way to bend them. Wrap tightly and bend the tips over the hair closest to the scalp. There are a few videos on YouTube that can help show you how to wrap your hair using curling rods of any kind, if you want to see it in action.

The rods are long and have a nice, slightly grippy texture on the surface, which is good for gripping the hair a little. But it's not too grippy that it would prevent easy removal from the curled hair.

They have a bit of cushioning to them, too, which means there's a little bit of give to them when you curl. The cushioning is also handy if you sleep in them. In general, it's not great sleeping with stuff stuck to your head. I managed to avoid getting a headache when I slept in these, though, which surprised me.

The ends are covered with little caps that keep the wire inside, and they kind of pop out of the rods a little, but not off. You can easily pop them back into place without any problems.

There are 6 of each size/color in the pack (7 sizes!) and you can choose a differing variety every time you set your hair, for differing looks. I have shoulder length hair and liked the smaller ones for the shortest hair at the nape of the neck, and graduate to larger sizes toward the top of my head. But I have used larger ones all around as well. It depends what kinds of curls you're going for. You can also use larger or smaller sections of hair to wrap each rod, for more variations.

The design of the clear/blue carrying case was also a factor in my decision. I like the upright design, the little zipper cap, and the handle on top. It's compact for the quantity of rods it contains, which makes it easy to travel with, though the vertical design can be difficult for getting all the rods back in and fitting well. It helps to straighten out the rods before putting them back in the container. Not a big deal, just a small struggle if you're short on time.

I have gotten crazy curly results from these after sleeping in these the other night. I was so curly I didn't recognize myself in the mirror! These rods will deliver! The key is to wrap moistened, but not sopping wet hair, wrap tightly and consistently. Mind those pesky ends and make sure they are held under the hair in the right direction, and leave these rods in for several hours until the hair is all completely dry. Overnight is best, but I've seen results in just a couple hours with only slightly dampened hair.

I'm still learning how to best curl using these, but I'm very happy with my investment. I think you will enjoy playing with your hair using these.

title: Top of the line razor...Great for shaving those hard to reach places
text:
I recently received the Philips Norelco arcitec 1090 razor and overall I have been very pleased. Before I got this razor, I used an older, less expensive Norelco razor, so I was excited to see if this one would be any better. I was not disappointed.

This is one of the more expensive Norelcos, so I expected everything about it to be high quality. There are many nice features to this razor. The front of the razor has a digital display telling you how many minutes are left (out of about 65 minutes fully charged) until your battery goes out, which even works while the razor is charging so you know exactly how much the battery is charged. After you use the razor, there is a little indicator light that goes on that reminds you to clean out the razor heads. Also, the charging base that is included is very nice and sturdy.

However, one of my favorite features is the traveling case that comes with the razor. This case is a hard plastic pod that fits securely around the razor. The pod even has a plug-in for the AC adapter so you can charge your razor while it is still in the case. For some reason the razor does not fit in the case with the plastic cover for the heads on, which seemed a bit strange to me, but not that big of a deal.

As far as shaving goes, this razor works as well or better as any other electric razor I have used. I've read some reviews complaining about razor burns with this razor, but in my experience this has not been a problem. On my old Norelco, the three razor heads would bend in toward the center when pressured. This razor is just the opposite: the razor heads bend outward on the springy flexible neck part of the razor. In the box is the callus remover, a little cleaning brush, the charging cord, and an extra pumice roller. The callus remover is about 6 inches long and fits really nicely in your hand. If your feet have a lot of tough skin, this little machine will generate a lot of skin dust. I would suggest using it over a towel or somewhere that is easy to clean up.

This is not a quiet tool. Not as loud as a blender, but definitely louder than, say a fan. It's probably about the same noise level as an electric toothbrush, maybe a little louder.

Two feet and 20 minutes later, I'm amazed with how smooth my feet are. I had some really bad cracking on one of my heels and now it's very smooth. I can't even feel or see the crack any longer.

title: How I got my feet in fab shape
text:
This thing is an essential step I took in getting my feet back to tip top shape. Being a dancer, my poor feet were doomed to have calluses. I do my best to avoid that at all costs, but I couldn't stop it. I ended up having a couple small ones and one decently thick one. This thing is amazing, especially for the smaller ones. Let's go right into a pro's and con's list.

pro's:
- Safely grinds away the skin
- Long battery life
- Can still be used while charging
- Long life for the stone (I got mine in February and still haven't needed a replacement with relatively frequent use)
- Strong motor that doesn't lag when touched to the skin (unless of course you're smashing it up against yourself which if you are.. stop.)

con's
- Take's a long time, especially for larger calluses (we will revisit this issue in a second)
- Does (of course) produce a fine, skin powder that is pretty gross if you think too hard about it. So don't think too hard about it.

Ok so now you've read the pro's and con's list and you might be wondering, "Adina, didn't you say you had a larger callus? Did you just end up spending days and weeks and years just to shave it off?"
The answer is no. While this tool was extremely helpful, I am much too impatient for that. As I mentioned, this foot file does take forever, but don't hate on it for that! You don't want a foot file that is too powerful or else it may take skin off in chunks rather than that lovely skin powder we discussed and thus your skin will no longer be soft and smooth which is, to my understanding, our goal.
Back to the issue of my larger callus. Here are the steps I took to remove that bad boy.

I started off just using the same method I used for the littler ones which was file for about an hour every other day in hopes that I could one day grind it down to the bottom. I don't like using this for much longer in only one spot as the skin begins to feel quite warm and I can't imagine that is good for you. After finishing up any areas that concern you, thickly apply O'Keeffe's [[ASIN:B0002QB9NE O'Keeffe's for Healthy Feet, Foot Cream 3.2oz]] and throw on some thick cotton socks. I'm sure this method would eventually work for the larger one too, but who has time for that? So I took an extra step with the large one and used Dr. Scholl's Medicated Callus remover [[ASIN:B00099XL30 Dr. Scholl's Callus Removers, Medicated, 6 pads]]. I put one on for 48 hours and when I took it off, the callused skin was very white and soft, but still there. I figured it was a bust but I went to the water park the next day and the mixture off water and walking around barefoot made most of the now-white and soft callus just come off. (Don't worry, it didn't come off in the water and I was able to throw the skin away properly) I'm sure you don't need to go to the water park to achieve the same goal, just give yourself a good foot soak and then scrub it away!
There was still a bit of callused skin underneath what came off but I was able to easily come back in with this foot file and finish it off! Now my feet are baby soft just in time for summer!

title: The Best In My Book!
text:
I have ready many user reviews and some technical reviews on the Norelco Arcitec and it has brought me to three conclusions: 1) You can't please everyone but you CAN please most 2) Some of the reviews must have been written by the competition and 3) A little more attention to detail will help some of you understand the product better.

I have been mostly a blade man for about 25 years, having only made a few brief attempts at using an electric. For the past several years, I have been using the Gillette Mach 3 and now the Fusion razors. They are the best blades ever, give a quick close shave and cost so much money to replace ($28.99 msrp for 8 blades), that if I changed them out when I really should (weekly is ideal and almost necessary they go dull so fast), I will have paid for the Norelco Arcitec 1050 plus a little extra, in just one year of use.

In the interest of trying something new, I have tried electrics before. I tried Norelco's first generation of the Nivea wet shaver and it was great, though it did run out of Nivea fast, which was hard to find and expensive and then I got bored and distracted and stopped using it almost as quickly as I started. BUT, it is still a work horse and whenever I break it out of retirement, and it still does a great job, even with worn out blades.

So, I decided to give the Arcitec a try. First, everyone comments on design and style, so let's get that out of the way. Great, innovative, light, maneuverable, and incredibly effective. I am NOT a dry shave guy. I only do it out of necessity when I am in a hurry. I have always found that wet shaving, even with my other Norelco which can do either, was WAYYY better and more comfortable. But, this is enough to convert me in just one use. Quick, smooth, effect, close, comfortable.

Let's debunk a couple of design complaints I have read about in previous reviews...

The trimmer...Yes, the trimmer may be a bit small, but I have a small face, and I almost never use a trimmer, so no biggie. BUT, one of the complaints I have read several times is that placement is bad because "you end up cutting your hair with the razor when you try to use the trimmer". People... the razor head pops off! Just pull it off when you are using the trimmer. It's pretty obvious you are supposed to. Which leads me to...

Replacing the blades...Other's have complained that you can't replace the blades, just the entire head from the neck up and that appears to be true. One user even said it costs almost as much as a new razor. Rubbish! It's $33 and change on Amazon for a new razor head. It will probably be less by the time any of us actually need to buy replacements. When was the last time you replaced the blades in an electric razor (O.K., a GOOD electric razor) for under $30? Assuming you do it once a year, you will pay what yo would for one 8 pack of Fusion blades.

Cleaning the blades... you have to open three small slots, instead pushing one button for one big chamber. It takes three seconds, so what?

There isn't a big hair chamber... Again, so what? I always hated having a bunch of hair gather in my razor.

The battery supposedly can be damaged by over charging, unlike previous models. Most likely, Norelco is just being careful. The nature of lithium ion and lithium polymer batteries is that they CAN'T be over charged, they have no burn in memory, and are safe to leave in the charge at all times. Even my old first-gen Norelco Nivea razor with cheap NiCad batteries, could be left in the charger forever and it never burned and still holds a charge for months or even years. You can take the risk and leave it in the charger. I did it all afternoon and evening yesterday with no notable problems.

One last observation, and I'm not the first one to make it... The only difference between the 1050, 1060 and 1090 razors is the LED. Each one offers a little more detail than the rest, but costs noticeably more for that detail. In all other ways each razor is the same. Maybe it's just me, but why pay up to $100 more for a unit that does all the same things? I don't care if mine has an LED that says I have 65 minutes left.

So, nutshell... great design, great performance, great everything. Take negative opinions with a grain of salt. With a 60 day return policy to Norelco, it's worth a trial run. I've only had it for a day and I already like it enough to keep it.

By the way, if you like wet shaving, it looks like it can do that too.

title: BEST SHAMPOO I HAVE USED TO DATE
text:
This nourishing shampoo contains all natural ingredients and lots of wonderful oils such as Argan, Peach, Avocado, Jojoba, Camelia and Almond oil so it cleans your hair without drying. Their special formula has been clinically proven to repair hair damage and reverse the effects of heat, excess styling and split ends. IT's the ultimate hair care experience. The unique blend of all-natural ingredients fortifies your hair from root to tip and makes it harder to damage your hair. It makes your hair stronger and less prove to breakage.

I have reviewed many shampoos in the past. That's why I figured, for the purpose of this review entry, to answer the 9 biggest shampoo questions that are asked.

HOW OFTEN SHOULD I SHAMPOO

There's no harm in washing your hair everyday, unless you start to see a lot of breakage. The whole process of wetting, drying your hair takes a lot of moisture out of it. So, here's a rule of thumb:
Wash your hair every day if you have oily hair, live in a polluted city, humid environment or work out every day.
Wash every other day if your hair is normal or combination.
Wash your hair every few days if your hair is on the dry side, you live in a rural environment or dry climate.

IS IT POSSIBLE TO USE TOO MUCH SHAMPOO

As long as you rinse it all out, you really can't use too much. A dollop the size of a quarter is usually enough, but hair length is also a factor. Lather can be drying, but since it only sits on your hair a few minutes, it's safe for all hair types.

WHAT IS THE IDEAL WATER TEMPERATURE

Warm water will work up a nice lather and help dissolve the soap so that your hair rinses clean. Avoid really hot water, which can make your hair limp. For the final rinse, cold water is best, it will help lock helpful ingredients into each strand and leave your hair shinier.

DOES SHAMPOO EXPIRE

Most shampoos have a shelf life of 2-3 years. A product that's older won't harm your hair, but it won't be as effective. A telltale sign is separation and/or a change in color or smell.

IF I PROTECT COLOR CAN I GET SHINE & VOLUME

Most shampoos that preserve color now include 'bonus' ingredients to promote volume and shine. If that's not enough for you, start a shampoo 'wardrobe'. Make the color protector your basic, but use the others on alternate days to get different benefits.

HOW OFTEN SHOULD I USE CLARIFYING SHAMPOO

If you use a lot of styling products, live in an area with mineral-rich water or swim a lot, you should use a clarifying shampoo twice a month. Oily types: Use a daily clarifying shampoo every time you wash. For the rest: Use a clarifying formula if your hair looks dull or has become resistant to your regular products.

ARE SALON SHAMPOOS BETTER THAN DRUGSTORE

Shampoo is not a 'you get what you pay for' product. There are a few factors you should know: Drugstore brands put a lot of money in their research and new technology. They keep their prices low because they manufacture mass quantities. Expensive shampoos have advantages of their own: They're gentler and contain a higher concentration of high-quality ingredients. So don't focus on the price tag, but on finding a formula that works for you.

WHEN IS IT BEST TO SWITCH SHAMPOO

Sometimes the same bottle can make your hair lackluster without warning. Unless the label alerts you to a 'new' or 'improved' formula it's the surface of your hair that's changed. First clarify your hair, then bring back your shampoo. No improvement? It may be time to switch for good. A simple test: Look at your nails. If they are ridged, peeling or break easily, you're just aging. This leads to water loss in your cells and tissues. Your hair may be dryer so buy a moisturizing version or ask your stylist to diagnose your new needs.

DO I NEED CONDITIONER

Conditioner is essential. It finishes what shampoo starts in terms or making your hair manageable and repairing split ends. You may go through many conditioners before you find the right one, but you'll know when you've met your match. When your hair is properly conditioned, it holds style better.

Now that I was able to answer some of the most frequently asked questions for you, I highly recommend this shampoo. It's great for all hair types, including color treated hair. I also enjoy their dedication to finding and researching the best ingredients to use in their products. For that reason, if you're ever unsatisfied, they'll make it right for you.

Why is Tamanu oil beneficial and good for skin?:

"Common Name: Tamanu

Calophyllum inophyllum

The Dr. Oz Show demonstrating the benefits of Tamanu Oil. Dr. Mehmet Oz is an informed and supportive advocate of the safe use of effective botanical remedies. He allows ample time for the health benefits of these botanicals to be presented in a clear and positive way.

The exotic isles of the South Pacific are home to a long-used traditional ingredient which is just now working its way into the US and European topical and cosmetic industries. Since the 1920’s Oil of Tamanu (Calophyllum inophyllum) has been studied in hospitals and by researchers in Europe, Asia and the Pacific islands. The results of this research are impressive. In 1999 and 2000, I travelled to the South Pacific to study the tamanu tree, and the processing of its oil, and delved into its science in earnest. This is what I learned.

Tamanu’s Healing Powers

Tamanu oil possesses a unique capacity to promote the formation of new tissue, thereby accelerating wound healing and the growth of healthy skin. This process is known as cicatrization. For this reason, it is a widely used traditional topical aid. In Pacific island folk medicine, tamanu oil is applied liberally to cuts, scrapes, burns, insect bites and stings, abrasions, acne and acne scars, psoriasis, diabetic sores, anal fissures, sunburn, dry or scaly skin, blisters, eczema, herpes sores, and to reduce foot and body odor. Tamanu oil is also massaged into the skin to relieve neuralgia, rheumatism and sciatica. Tamanu oil is employed by Polynesian women for promoting healthy, clear, blemish-free skin, and is also used on babies to prevent diaper rash and skin eruptions.

Tamanu and Its Dispersal

Calophyllum inophyllum is indigenous to Southeast Asia, but is profuse in Polynesia. The tree grows up to 25 or even 30 meters in height, with long, spreading limbs. The tree trunk is typically thick with dark, cracked bark. The tamanu branches are covered with shiny, dark green oval leaves, and small white flowers with yellow centres. The blossoms give off a delightful, sweet perfume. The fruit of the tree, about the size of an apricot, has a thin flesh and a large nut hull inside.

Yet the tamanu nut is a botanical oddity. When the fruits of the tree are collected and cracked open, the blond nut kernel inside contains no apparent oil. But when the kernel dries on a rack for a month or so, it turns a deep, chocolate brown, and becomes sticky with a rich, pleasant-smelling oil. Using a simple screw press, the oil is squeezed from the dark kernels. The resulting oil of tamanu is dark green and luxurious. Though oil of tamanu is thick and rich, once it is applied to skin it is readily and completely absorbed, leaving no oily residue.

“Tamanu oil possesses a unique capacity to promote the formation of new tissue, thereby accelerating wound healing and the growth of healthy skin. This process
is known as cicatrization.” - Chris Kilham
Anti-Neuralgic and Skin Healing Activity

Traditionally oil of tamanu has enjoyed topical use in Fiji for relieving the pain of sciatica, shingles, neuralgia, rheumatism and leprous neuritis, for which it is effective. In 1918, researchers associated with the French Pharmacopoeia began research into tamanu for topical and subcutaneous use. The French researchers quickly became impressed by tamanu’s cicatrizing properties. In the French medical literature on tamanu oil, several instances of its successful use in cases of severe skin conditions have been reported. In one remarkable instance, a woman was admitted to the St. Louis Hospital in Paris with a large gangrenous ulcer on her leg which would not heal. Though doctors were sure that amputation was inevitable, she was given regular dressings of tamanu oil. The wound healed completely, leaving a smooth, flat scar. In other cases, tamanu oil has been employed successfully to heal severe burns caused by boiling water, chemicals and X-rays.

Novel Constituents in Tamanu Oil

Oil of tamanu contains three basic classes of lipids, neutral lipids, glycolipids, and phospholipids. The oil also contains a unique fatty acid called calophyllic acid, and a novel antibiotic lactone and non-steroidal anti-inflammatory agent called calophyllolide. These and other components of tamanu oil, including anti-inflammatory coumarins, account for some of the oil’s beneficial activity.

Based on the known activity of known constituents, it is clear that oil of tamanu possesses antibacterial and anti-inflammatory activities. The unique cicatrizing properties of tamanu oil are not yet explained in existing scientific literature, though this activity is established and accepted. The same is true for tamanu’s anti-neuralgic properties. Tamanu oil is well documented for its relief of neuritis, but the constituents responsible and their modes of activity are not yet known.
Product Applications

Oil of tamanu is suitable for general skin and cosmetic purposes. The oil’s unusual absorption, its mild and pleasant aroma, and its luxurious feel make it ideal for use in lotions, creams, ointments and other cosmetic products. Considering that tamanu is a potent healing agent with proven benefits, it is only a matter of time before tamanu breaks through to more widespread use, and assumes a position among other successful topical and cosmetic ingredients."

title: OK, but outperformed by a $10 foil electric
text:
I got this shaver in early January of 2007. For the first month or so that I had it, it worked decently. The shave was relatively close and it did get most of the hair, but it did take a few passes over the skin, and a touch-up using the on-board trimmer to get the ones it missed. I also found myself having the stretch the skin quite a bit to get a close enough shave. However, it did offer an irritation-free shave (I have sensitive skin, thus why I stay away from blade razors).

Over the next few months, though, I noticed that the shave started to get more irritating: more 'pulling' instead of cutting (had always pulled a little, but got more frequent), takes more passes to cut what it once would, etc. I changed the blades after 3 months (short period, yes, but I tried anyway). It helped a little, but it still wasn't as good as it once was. Then, I started to realize that the shaver wasn't holding as strong a charge as it once did. It would come off the charger and be 'full power' for less than one shave, and would need to go back on the charger after 6 shaves (far less than the advertised two weeks). A call to Norelco led nowhere, as they said it was 'expected' for the battery to wear down over time (4 months?).

I kept using the razor as I wasn't about to waste the $90 investment. On a trip in late July, I had forgotten to pack the shaver, so I purchased a $10 Remington battery-operated foil razor at a local convenience store. Sad to say, but from Day 1 that foil razor has outperformed the Norelco by leaps and bounds in all areas (closer shave, gets all areas better, less passes needed, etc.). Also on a sad note, the Remington is kicking the bucket (a year later), and I am forced to go back to the Norelco for the time being while I look for an acceptable foil shaver as a replacement.

In short, this razor performed decently at first, but it seems as though compared to a $10 battery operated razor, this $70 shaver isn't a good value for the investment.

I've also always found the taste extremely mild. Never bothered me. The texture is different from normal toothpaste in that it doesn't foam, but I feel you brush better this way! You actually feel a lot more of your teeth and gums while you brush.

Give it a try!

title: Miniature Bath Brush - Misleading description
text: This is a sweet miniature bath brush - and the description is very misleading. It does not have a long handle, and it is not nonslip. Everything about it is tiny, from the scrubber brush to the handle length.  The brush is a small circle  which prevents a user from doing much scrubbing without moving the brush around a lot.  Unfortunately,  while the short handle seems to be made of a durable material, it is very smooth and will slip out of soapy hands easily. From the awkward wording in some of the reviews praising the generous size of the brush, I have to wonder if they were written by friends of the seller!  The bristles are soft but firm, and feel nice to the touch, but that is the only good thing to say about the brush.  I just wish there were enough of them to get the job done without having to jockey the brush back and forth and spend so much time picking it up from the shower floor.

title: Scent is Overpowering
text:
Let me start by saying I love french-milled soaps. I love scented soap. I love guest/sample size soaps. I adore the delightful concept and packaging design of this set. It was on my wish list and I received it as a gift. I was looking very forward to having these soaps to add some holiday cheer to my home.

Here's what happened. The person that purchased it for me was so overwhelmed by the strong scent that he had to triple bag the box and store it in a vacant room until Christmas. Each soap is individually wrapped. They're wrapped in plastic. Then in a box. Then they're double bagged in two ziploc bags. Then placed in yet another box, wrapped with wrapping paper. The box was under my tree for two days, and scent still managed to seep out and perfume all the other gifts under the tree nearby - but not in a pleasant way. When this was unwrapped Christmas morning it was so unbelievably overpowering my eyes watered. I didn't even bother to look closely at them - I could not get them back inside their ziplocs fast enough. People got headaches and complained loudly.. The entire downstairs smelled like a soap factory instead of the fresh cinnamon rolls I baked for Christmas morning. The soaps are now safely contained in their hazmat bags and stored in the laundry room instead of the guest bath. :(

I'm really kind of bummed about this because I was so excited about these soaps. I want to try them or at least take them out and smell each one on its own, but I'm afraid to now.

Greenwich Bay, if you read these reviews: please, please, PLEASE turn the scent levels down several notches in the recipe for these soaps. I think the scent must develop stronger as the soaps "ripen" because it's just much too much. Way more than any other french milled soaps I own.

title: If you are pregnant, you will love this!
text:

title: Disappointed-Product Stopped Working After 4 Months
text:
I received the foot file on 24 April and began using it several days later. It worked well, I was pleased with its removal of calloused skin and used it about once per week. In July/August I noticed it took longer to charge the device. I did not drop the device and I cleaned it as instructed in the accompanying brochure.
On 4 September I picked up the device to use it. I pressed it against my skin, and the roller fizzled. The roller then stopped turning. I tried recharging the device without success.
It is completely dead and cannot be revived.
When I turn it on, the device does absolutely nothing. When I plug it into the charger, the light is green indicating the device is fully charged.
I ordered an extra set of rollers expecting the device to last longer than 4 months. I am disappointed it is not a reliable product. Based on the short life of this product, I cannot recommend it.

title: This stuff actually works!
text:
I had a pretty ugly blackhead on my nose. For weeks I tried everything to get rid of it. I even asked my girlfriend for some beauty tips. Nothing worked. After awhile I noticed it getting bigger so I became desperate. I did something most guys would ever do... I visited a beauty salon that specializes in skin care. Fortunately for me, the lady I spoke to didn't want to take my money and told me to just pick up a bottle of Vi-Tae Blackhead remover. She told me all this mombo jumbo about why and how it works and I pretended like I understood but it all flew over my head. I went home later that night and found it on Amazon. Honestly, I didn't want to spend $30+ dollars on a health and beauty product because, well, I'm a guy. But I took the lady's advice and went with it. Like Prime normally does, I got it in two days. I followed the directions - apply every morning to damp skin, let it sit for a few minutes and rinse. I have to be honest... I didn't see any difference after the first day. The blackhead was still there. I did it again the second day. Nothing. Third day. Zilch. Fourth day. Nada. I was becoming impatient and felt ripped off. However, after I applied it on the fifth day, the blackhead was gone after I rinsed it! I was like WHOA! This girly stuff really works. Before I start to rave about this stuff, I have to say that it didn't get it all out. If I look close enough, I can still see a tiny spec left in my pore. But I'll just continue using this stuff and see what happens. In all honesty, no one else can see it anymore. But my girlfriend said to continue keeping it clean so it doesn't come back.

FYI, I'm a 31 year old Asian male with pretty oily skin.

PROS:
- Actually works but it can take up to a week to remove a large blackhead
- Smells good and refreshing
- Directions are easy to follow

CONS:
- This stuff will sting the first few times you use it. It's not unbearable but it's pretty annoying
- It's a tad difficult to rinse off after you let it sit for a few minutes

title: BUY THESE - what is $1.88 anyway?
text:

You'll have to wait longer for it, but just know that this isn't inferior to the more expensive ones - there is no difference whatsoever.

A few months ago, I reviewed the same product by another brand (Foxnovo) and after reviewing it, went in search to see if there were others selling for less. That is when I found and ordered this one, as well as a pair from every brand, in every price point. I haven't noticed any difference at all between the Foxnovo and this one, or any of them for that matter.

I have a moderate looking, but excruciatingly painful feeling bunion. I am to the point of desperation, and have tried anything and everything I think might help. It's not magic, but my toe has felt much better in the months since I've been wearing it. I like it well enough that I'm even just wearing it around the house under my sock. If it's on right, I don't even notice it's there.

It's thick enough to provide *some* amount of support between the big toe and the second toe, but it's soft and squishy enough that it doesn't bulk up my foot too much to wear shoes. It's really soft and comfy feeling also.

There are a few reviewers here and on other similar products that complain that it cuts off circulation in their toe. I don't understand this at all. Are they putting it on wrong? :-/ I wear a woman's size 10, and have kind of fat feet. This fits nicely, and would also fit for smaller feet because it's stretchy and it stretches to get around my toe. I can't speak for bigger feet than mine, however. I suppose it could reach the point of cutting off circulation, but I really think if you put it on right, it won't reach that point easily.

You might be so desperate that you can't wait for this product to arrive from China. There are other options selling for $8.99 Prime-shipped. Go ahead and buy a pair and see if you like them. If they help the pain, that price is fine too. If you end up liking those, I promise these are the same exact thing, and maybe you'll then want to stock up by buying a whole bunch of these. They might not be the most attractive footwear, but the amount they have decreased my bunion pain is so significant that I don't ever want to live without them again.

title: Quality commensurate with price, but beware sizes
text:
The sizes on these are strange. People's fingers vary a lot in size, obviously, and this is a set without any specific sizing information, so I didn't expect them to necessarily fit all my fingers correctly. But the way they didn't fit was surprising. The largest two barely fit on my thumb--if I push it down enough not to fall off, it cuts off my circulation. The smallest two fit on my pinky well, maybe a little small. The others, which you'd expect to be between those sizes...well, they are between those two sizes, but they're almost as big as the thumb ones. A person with a thumb that size...there's just no way their ring, middle, and pointer fingers would be that huge.

Anyway, it's better for them to be too big than too small. If you push them down they don't look good, but grab something similar to foam mounting tape (https://www.amazon.com/3M-Heavy-Mounting-1-Inch-50-Inch/dp/B00004Z4A8) and pad the top inside of the rings that are too big. It makes them more comfortable, too!

That makes the only problem child in my set the thumb.
